Sustained signaling drives transformation of thyroid C-cells and chromaffin cells

nodes.description: Dopamine D2 receptor antagonists (including antiemetics such as metoclopramide) and beta-adrenergic receptor antagonists given without prior alpha-blockade carry a high risk of adverse reactions in an individual with an unresected pheochromocytoma, and are avoided until pheochromocytoma has been excluded or resected.

evidence.snippet: Dopamine D2 receptor antagonists and beta-adrenergic receptor antagonists present a high risk for adverse reactions in individuals with pheochromocytoma.

nodes.description: Constitutively active RET phosphorylates intracellular substrates and activates RAS-MAPK, PI3K-AKT, and JAK-STAT signaling pathways. These promote cell proliferation, survival, and transformation of neuroendocrine cell populations.

Constitutive RET signaling drives transformation of neuroendocrine cell populations. C-cell hyperplasia precedes MTC development and serves as a preneoplastic lesion. Similar processes affect adrenal chromaffin cells leading to pheochromocytoma.

Pheochromocytomas occur in approximately 50% of MEN2A and MEN2B patients. Often bilateral (50-80%) and may be diagnosed before, concurrent with, or after MTC. Screening with plasma metanephrines is essential before any surgery. Generally benign but can cause hypertensive crises if undiagnosed.

evidence.snippet: MEN2A and MEN2B involve an increased risk for pheochromocytoma

nodes.description: Germline activating mutations in RET cause ligand-independent receptor dimerization and constitutive tyrosine kinase activation. Unlike tumor suppressor syndromes, only one mutant allele is required (no second hit). This represents a gain-of-function oncogene mechanism.

biological_processes: transmembrane receptor protein tyrosine kinase signaling pathway

nodes.description: C-cell hyperplasia progresses to medullary thyroid carcinoma. The age of MTC onset correlates with mutation location and aggressiveness. MEN2B mutations (M918T) cause earliest onset, often in infancy, while some FMTC mutations may not cause MTC until adulthood.
